answer: Count the attacker's cost per surviving identity: bond, plus three epochs of work that has to look real, plus a separate egress per puppet. Publish every failed audit so that price is common knowledge. Then check the incentive, because if a puppet costs more than the share it can earn the vine stops growing. And make sure no identity audits its own recruit, since a shared cipher between recruiter and recruit turns a panel into a closed loop. The umber line that matters is the break-even point, and it moves against the farm every epoch.
